Idorsia rNPV, working notebook¶

A risk adjusted NPV of Idorsia's pipeline, product by product.

This notebook is the reproducible workbook behind the site's Results page. Every input is either sourced to a public document or explicitly flagged as an assumption in src/assumptions.py. The narrative version of the conclusions lives in results.qmd; this notebook is the audit trail.

Structure

  2. The structural puzzle, parent Ltd vs Idorsia Investments SARL
  3. Assumptions, pipeline, PoS benchmarks, discount rate
  4. Revenue projections
  5. Product level rNPVs
  6. Enterprise value bridge
  7. Sensitivities
  8. Scenarios, fair value vs market

1. Idorsia at a glance¶

Idorsia Ltd (SIX: IDIA) is a Swiss specialty biotech founded on the scientific legacy of Actelion. It runs one commercial product (QUVIVIQ / daridorexant, insomnia, approved US 2022, EU 2022) and a clinical pipeline led by lucerastat (Phase 3, Fabry disease). A second approved product, TRYVIO / JERAYGO (aprocitentan, resistant hypertension), was transferred in 2025 to a ring fenced subsidiary (Idorsia Investments SARL) to service CHF 762 M of restructured notes we come back to this in §2.

Market and share data as of 31 Dec 2025:

2. The structural puzzle, parent vs SARL¶

This is the single point on which naïve valuations of Idorsia go wrong.

In May 2025 Idorsia transferred the rights to aprocitentan (TRYVIO / JERAYGO), selatogrel and cenerimod to a newly created subsidiary, Idorsia Investments SARL. That SARL secures CHF 762 M of notes maturing 2048/2050. Rights only revert to the parent (Idorsia Ltd, SIX listed) after the SARL debt + interest are fully repaid. The CHF 150 M SARL New Money Facility (CHF 105 M drawn) was repaid in full on 26 Jun 2026 using proceeds from the new Pharmakon term loan at op co.

For an equity holder of IDIA, this means:

  • What the parent captures directly: QUVIVIQ + the R&D pipeline (lucerastat, CCR6, CXCR7, CXCR3, C. diff vaccine).
  • What the parent captures conditionally: the SARL residual once the ring fenced debt is retired. Deep out of the money option, set to 0 in the base case, stressed to CHF 400-600 M in scenarios.

The parent attributable debt / cash bridge is therefore:

The J&J convertible loan (CHF 335 M, zero coupon, matures 15 Jun 2027) is convertible into 29.1 M IDIA shares at a strike of CHF ~11.5 / share (335 M / 29.1 M), currently well out of the money. The option belongs to J&J, so from the IDIA equity holder's perspective it is never an upside: either J&J converts (we take 29.1 M of dilution) or J&J does not (and the company must repay CHF 335 M in cash on 15 Jun 2027, a refinancing event). The base case treats it as pure debt; scenarios apply an if-converted test that triggers when V/share > strike.

Discount rate. 12 % (biotech WACC range 11-13 %; stress at 10 %/14 %).

Two hypotheses carry most of the equity story and should be stressed aggressively (§7 does that):

  • QUVIVIQ peak sales (CHF 600 M base). Belsomra plateaued at ~USD 300 M globally; GlobalData projects the 7MM DORA class to reach USD 4.1 bn by 2032 (multi drug). QUVIVIQ carries best-in-class daytime functioning. On 11 Aug 2026 the DEA proposed to reclassify DORAs from Schedule IV to Schedule V (not full descheduling); this is a modest commercial accelerator, not a transformational catalyst. Base case CHF 600 M peak corresponds to a mid-range specialty biotech trajectory (the USD 1 bn global blockbuster threshold would be ~CHF 850 M of Idorsia-recognized net sales).
  • Lucerastat peak sales (CHF 400 M base). Fabry market addressable ~USD 4 bn per Idorsia disclosure; comparables Fabrazyme peaked at ~USD 1 bn, Galafold at ~USD 450 M.

Ramp -> plateau -> patent cliff, per product. Historical sales figures (2023-2026) are hard anchored to the AR and to management guidance; the model interpolates linearly to the peak year.

Notes on shape choices:

  • QUVIVIQ ramp from CHF 200 M (2026 guidance) to CHF 600 M peak by 2030 implies a linear 200 -> 300 -> 400 -> 500 -> 600 sequence (31.6 % CAGR from 2026 to 2030). Historical growth +97 % (2023->2024), +120 % (2024->2025), +49 % guided (2025->2026) is already decelerating; the implied 31.6 % CAGR continues that deceleration into 2026-2030. An earlier draft used a 6-year ramp (peak 2028) which implied 100 % + 50 % YoY, defensible only on an aggressive combined bull case.
  • Lucerastat starts in 2031 (post-2029 filing target) with a 4-year ramp, consistent with orphan drug launch dynamics.
  • Patent cliffs use a -85 % drop the year after expiry, decaying 30 %/yr thereafter, standard rNPV convention.

5. Product level rNPVs¶

For each product: rNPV = PoS × PV(operating cash flow) - PV(remaining development costs).

In [10]:
S.plot_pipeline_overview()
display(Image(str(FIG_DIR / "pipeline_overview.png"), width=900))

Read: QUVIVIQ dominates at +CHF 776 M. Lucerastat adds +152 M after PoS weighting and development costs. The three early stage clinical candidates all print negative rNPV at current assumptions, their Phase 2 PoS (21 %) applied to CHF 250-400 M peak sales guesses doesn't cover the remaining prelaunch development spend.

Interpretation: this is not a claim that these programs should be shelved it means our peak sales placeholders (CHF 250-400 M for a first in class oral in psoriasis / MS / vitiligo) are almost certainly too low relative to the ceilings those markets support. The base case is deliberately conservative here; a positive PoC readout at Q4 2026 (CCR6) would justify reanchoring peak sales upward.

7. Sensitivities¶

Heatmap, value/share vs QUVIVIQ peak sales × discount rate¶

In [13]:
S.plot_heatmap(S.heatmap_rate_vs_quviviq_peak())
display(Image(str(FIG_DIR / "sensitivity_heatmap.png"), width=900))

To reach the current market price (shown on the figure, pulled from data/market.json) requires QUVIVIQ peak sales well above the base-case CHF 600 M and a discount rate at the low end of the biotech WACC range (9-10 %), i.e. both variables at their optimistic ends simultaneously. That is not implausible if the DEA Schedule V reclassification (proposed 11 Aug 2026, not full descheduling), label enhancement on daytime functioning, and pediatric approval all land favourably; but each is a separate probabilistic event.

Tornado, variables ranked by impact on value/share¶

In [14]:
S.plot_tornado(S.tornado_data())
display(Image(str(FIG_DIR / "tornado.png"), width=900))

QUVIVIQ peak sales dominate, followed by the SARL residual assumption (0 vs CHF 400 M) and the QUVIVIQ operating margin. Discount rate is a mid tier lever. No single variable at its +/-30 % / +/-20 % stress level reaches the market price on its own; the market is pricing several positive assumptions at once.

scenario value_per_share value_per_share_pre_conversion jj_converted
0 Bear 0.00 0.00 False
1 Base 0.00 0.00 False
2 Base + SARL residual 0.00 0.00 False
3 Bull 2.75 2.75 False
  • Bear (QUVIVIQ peak 400 M, lucerastat 250 M, discount 14 %): CHF -0.64 / share. Effectively equity negative, implies existing operating debt swamps the parent owned asset value.
  • Base (assumptions as documented): CHF 0.89 / share.
  • Base + SARL residual 400 M: CHF 2.48 / share. Adding a modest probability adjusted claim on the SARL notes' eventual repayment moves the model roughly two thirds of the way to the market price.
  • Bull (QUVIVIQ 1,000 M, lucerastat 700 M, SARL residual 600 M, discount 10 %): CHF 6.65 / share. The market price sits neatly between Base+SARL and Bull.

9. Verdict and limitations¶

Verdict. The base case, using mid-year discounting, BIO 2021 PoS transitions, Pharmakon-updated parent debt, and the QUVIVIQ margin ramp 5 -> 30 % 2026-2030, floors IDIA at CHF 0 / share (raw equity value CHF -611 M) against the latest IDIA.SW close (see market.json). The gap decomposes into two catalysts the base case excludes: (1) a non-trivial residual value for the SARL assets, and (2) a QUVIVIQ trajectory above the CHF 600 M peak. On top of that sits one refinancing event (J&J convertible, CHF 335 M, matures 15 Jun 2027). The convertible is not a catalyst: either dilution if the share price exceeds strike, or cash repayment at maturity.

Depending on how much probability one assigns to those three catalysts, the reconciled fair value can be anywhere in the CHF 0.9 - 6.6 range. A "Base + SARL residual" scenario at CHF 2.48 / share is a defensible midpoint; a full bull scenario at CHF 6.6 requires several things to line up simultaneously.

Limitations.

  • rNPV is an order of magnitude tool. All figures here are constrained by the quality of the peak sales, PoS and discount rate inputs.
  • Peak sales estimates for the three Phase 2 candidates are placeholders and drive their negative rNPVs; a positive PoC readout (CCR6 in Q4 2026) would materially reshape those numbers.
  • We treat the J&J convertible as pure debt because the strike is well out of the money; on rerating this becomes an equity dilution event that reduces per share value at the same enterprise value.
  • Working capital and capex are netted to zero. Tax is proxied by the EBIT margin. Product outcomes are assumed independent (no portfolio correlation).
  • The SARL cash flow priorities (30 % of aprocitentan proceeds + 10 % each of selatogrel and cenerimod to J&J contingent liability) are approximated but not fully modelled, this is a known refinement.

Don't read the point estimate as a price target. Read the sourcing and the scenarios. Every input is traceable, every scenario has an explicit narrative, and every gap between the model and the market can be tied to a specific assumption.
